 The South Korean director and stars of the film coming to Netflix discuss its complex themes, from AI and labour issues to human connection
 4 -MIN READ 4 -MIN Listen James Mottram in London Published: 3:15pm, 3 Nov 2026 Updated: 4:09pm, 3 Nov 2026 Even by the high standards of contemporary Korean cinema and television, anticipation was palpable when Possible Love premiered at the Venice International Film Festival in September. The film marked the first release in eight years from Lee Chang-dong – the novelist, former politician and filmmaker whose previous work, the 2018 mystery drama Burning , was one of that year’s most critically acclaimed. Given that his preceding film, 2010’s Poetry , arrived another eight years prior, new Lee projects are rare events to be savoured. One might assume Lee spent the intervening years meticulously crafting Possible Love , given the screenplay’s layered complexity. Summarising it as a tale of two couples – one rich, one poor – barely scratches the surface.
